title: Cloning and Tracking a Shared Repository
description: Practice cloning and tracking a shared repository through a concrete team scenario.

blocks.content: When you join an existing project, you start by **cloning** the repository. Cloning creates a complete local copy of the project, including its entire history. It also automatically sets up the connection back to the original so you can push and pull.

## Cloning a Repository

Clone a repository from a URL:
```
git clone https://github.com/example/my-project.git
```

This creates a folder called `my-project` containing the project files and a `.git` folder with all the history. The original repository is automatically set as a remote called `origin`.

## Remote-Tracking Branches

After cloning, your local Git knows about the remote's branches. These are called **remote-tracking branches** and they look like `origin/main`. They are read-only snapshots of where the remote's branches were the last time you fetched.

See all branches including remote-tracking ones:
```
git branch -a
```

Update your remote-tracking branches with the latest from the server:
```
git fetch origin
```

## Connecting an Existing Repo to a Remote

If you already have a local repo and want to connect it to a remote:
```
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourname/your-project.git
git push -u origin main
```

The `-u` flag sets `origin/main` as the default for future `git push` and `git pull` commands.

blocks.question: What does `git clone` create on your machine?
options: Only the latest version of the files, with no history
A complete local copy of the repository including all its history
A shortcut that reads files directly from the server
A zip file of the current branch
blocks.explanation: `git clone` copies the entire repository - all files, all branches, and the complete commit history - onto your machine. You can then work offline and push changes back when you're ready.

blocks.prompt: Clone the repository at https://github.com/example/repo.git into the current folder.
